resources.string: Play the white pieces and try to trap the black king (checkmate). Tap one of your pieces to see where it can go, then tap a highlighted square, or drag the piece there. When a pawn reaches the far side, you choose what it becomes.\n\nPick a level at the bottom: Training, Standard or Expert against the computer, or Two players on the same screen. Wins against the computer give neutrinos. A game ends in a draw by stalemate, repetition, the fifty-move rule or too few pieces left. Your game is saved automatically.

You play the white pieces, the computer plays black. Tap a piece, then tap a highlighted square to move it. Pieces move one square diagonally forward and become kings on the last row; a king slides as far as it wants along a diagonal.\n\nCapturing is mandatory: jump over an enemy piece, forwards or backwards, and keep jumping if you can. When several captures are possible you must take the one that captures the most pieces. Capture or block all enemy pieces to win. Pick a level at the bottom, or play with two players. Wins against the computer give neutrinos.

Place a disc on an empty square so that it traps a line of enemy discs between your new disc and another one of yours, in any direction. The trapped discs flip to your colour. Tap one of the highlighted squares to play.\n\nIf you cannot play, your turn passes. The game ends when nobody can play; whoever has the most discs wins. You play white against the computer, or switch to two players with the mode button. A win against the computer gives neutrinos.

Build the four foundation piles from ace to king, one suit per pile. In the seven columns, stack cards in descending order, alternating red and black. Only a king can fill an empty column.\n\nTap a card (or a run of cards) and then its destination, or drag it there. Double-tap a card to send it to its foundation. Tap the stock pile to turn over one card; when it is empty, tap it again to flip the waste pile back. Use Undo to take back moves, and Auto finish appears when the game is won in practice. Winning gives neutrinos.

Flip two cards per turn. If they show the same picture, they stay face up; otherwise they flip back after a moment, so try to remember where they are. Find all the pairs to win.\n\nThe buttons at the top choose the grid size, from small to very large, and start a new game. The magnifier makes the cards bigger so you can scroll around the board. Your flips and time are counted and your best scores are kept. Winning gives neutrinos.

Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Number cards count their value, face cards count 10, and an ace counts 11 or 1. Choose your bet in neutrinos with the minus and plus buttons, then tap Deal. If you have no neutrinos left, you play for free.

Hit draws a card, Stand keeps your hand, Double doubles your bet for one last card, and Split separates two cards of the same value into two hands. The dealer draws until reaching 17. A winning hand pays your bet, a natural blackjack pays one and a half times, and a tie gives your bet back.

The gear lets you add 0 to 4 computer players at the table.

This is a slot machine with a 3 by 3 grid. Choose a bet in neutrinos, then tap Spin. The three columns stop one after the other.

You win when a row, a column or a diagonal shows three identical symbols: your bet is multiplied by 2. A rainbow star is a joker: with one joker the multiplier is 3, with two jokers 4, and three jokers in a line give 5. Several winning lines add their multipliers together. A line containing a black hole never wins.

You cannot choose a bet higher than your neutrino balance.
